title: Crohn's, ulcerative colitis, IBS and pancreatitis
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's digestive condition.
note:
Chief Complaint
Abdominal discomfort and bloating.

HPI
Pt is an 85-year-old female presenting for f/u of chronic GI symptoms. Pt reports persistent abdominal cramping and bloating, particularly after meals. She describes the pain as intermittent. She notes changes in bowel habits over the last several months. Pt underwent a colonoscopy recently which was normal. Based on the clinical presentation and negative endoscopic findings, pt is diagnosed with irritable bowel syndrome. Pt denies any acute changes in symptoms or significant weight loss.

Medication List
Lisinopril 10mg QD
Metformin 500mg BID
Atorvastatin 20mg QD

Review of Systems
Constitutional: Negative for fever, chills, or weight loss.
GI: Positive for bloating and cramping. Negative for nausea or vomiting.
CV: Negative for chest pain or palpitations.
Resp: Negative for SOB or cough.
MSK: Negative for joint pain.
Neuro: Negative for dizziness or syncope.

Social History
Pt is retired. Lives with her spouse. Non-smoker. No alcohol use.

Family History
Mother had hypertension. Father had type 2 diabetes.

Vitals
BP: 132/82
HR: 74 (RRR)
Temp: 98.6 F
SpO2: 97% on RA
Ht: 12.4 g/dL
WBC: 7.2_k
Glucose: 115 mg/dL
eGFR: 68 mL/min

Exam
General: Pt appears well, in no acute distress.
CV: RRR, regular rhythm.
Lungs: CTAB.
Abdomen: Soft, non-tender, non-distended. No guarding or rebound. Bowel sounds present.
Skin: Warm, dry, intact.
Neurological: Alert and oriented x3.

Assessment
1. Irritable bowel syndrome. Colonoscopy was normal. No evidence of organic pathology.

Plan
1. Continue current medications for hypertension and diabetes.
2. For IBS, pt to continue low-FODMAP diet as tolerated.
3. Provide reassurance regarding normal colonoscopy results.
4. F/u in 6 months or as needed for symptom exacerbation.

Electronically signed,
D. Kowalski, DO
05/14/2026
explanations: Irritable bowel syndrome: K58.9 (no HCC). It is not inflammatory bowel disease.

distractors.why: IBS is not ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease.
